lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Bloomberg Terminal
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Education appears before stronger professional finance experience.
items.because: It makes the résumé initially read like that of an early-career graduate.

items.says: The move from Financial Analyst to Caddie is unexplained.
items.because: The unrelated, less senior role may raise questions about career direction or why the finance role ended.

items.says: The current Caddie entry takes too much space at the top of a finance résumé.
items.because: Two bullets give an unrelated role weight comparable to relevant finance experience.

items.says: The older Student Investment Fund entry takes too much space.
items.because: Three bullets draw attention from more recent and senior evidence when only the benchmark report clearly supports the fund story.

items.says: The rounds-per-week figure reports workload without an outcome.
“Caddied” uses past tense for a current position.
“About 5 rounds a week” is unnecessarily wordy.
“Helped the pro shop run” leaves the candidate’s action and ownership undefined.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what responsibility the candidate handled.

items.says: The tournament bullet gives no scope or result.
items.because: The event label does not show the contribution’s significance.

items.says: “Helped” uses past tense for a duty in a current position.
items.because: It implies the responsibility ended or the dates are inaccurate.

items.says: “Close efficiency” does not define what improved by 40%.
items.because: The result is difficult to interpret or verify without the measure.

items.says: The automation tool or workflow is not identified.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what transferable technical skill produced the improvement.

items.says: The consistency of discount-rate and payback rules has no stated effect.
The clause about every request using the same rules is wordy.
The board-pack deliverable has no stated effect on reporting or decisions.
The bullet does not show how the variances were analyzed.
“Each line” could mean a line of text rather than a financial line item.
Discounting free cash flow to equity at WACC is technically wrong.
items.because: Free cash flow to equity requires the cost of equity; WACC applies to free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: The acquisition valuation’s effect on the transaction is unstated.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether it shaped a bid, negotiation, recommendation, or decision.

items.says: A group EBITDA margin cannot be calculated by adding business-unit margins.
items.because: Margins are ratios; the group margin uses consolidated EBITDA divided by consolidated revenue.

items.says: The 45% margin lacks a reporting period and comparator.
items.because: Without those anchors, its significance is hard to judge.

items.says: The margin bullet does not say what the result changed or informed.
“Monthly forecast error under 4%” does not identify the forecast output.
items.because: The accuracy claim is not interpretable or readily defensible.

items.says: The USD 40M early debt repayment is buried.
items.because: It is more consequential than the forecast’s scope and should be visible on a quick scan.

items.says: The strongest Stonebridge achievement appears last.
items.because: Its position reduces the chance a scanning reader sees the analyst’s best evidence of impact.

items.says: The underwriting bullet does not say how credit risk was assessed.
items.because: A credit hiring manager cannot tell which underwriting skills the candidate used.

items.says: “My findings” uses a first-person pronoun.
items.because: It breaks the action-phrase convention used by the surrounding bullets.

items.says: The approvals result is not placed first in the Crescent entry.
items.because: It shows both policy impact and risk control.

items.says: The review of declined applications does not identify the analysis behind the threshold changes.
items.because: The reader cannot distinguish systematic credit-policy analysis from a general file review.

items.says: “Writes” presents work at a role that ended in 2022 as ongoing.
items.because: Present tense contradicts the employment dates.

items.says: The checklist bullet does not identify what changed in monitoring.
items.because: The reader cannot tell which feature prevented missed tests.

items.says: The spreading template’s time-saving feature is unspecified.
items.because: The omission hides the technical skill responsible for the result.

items.says: “Cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3” treats the memo as a duration.
items.because: The figures measure preparation time, not the memo itself.

items.says: The market-price comparison lacks direction and an as-of date.
items.because: Without them, the 6% difference cannot be interpreted as upside or downside precisely.

items.says: The discount-rate change lacks direction, exact rates, and a clear meaning for “point.”
items.because: Those anchors are needed to interpret the change in share value.

items.says: The club’s spring-pitch use does not identify which part of the work it adopted.
The FP&A support bullet states no outcome.
items.because: It shows participation but no reporting improvement, decision, or other result.

items.says: “Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis” is too broad.
items.because: It does not identify the candidate’s action or a specific output.

items.says: The FP&A support bullet makes the investment-fund entry feel like mixed work.
items.because: It sounds like corporate finance work and dilutes the benchmark-report story.

items.says: The benchmark-report bullet does not appear first.
items.because: It is the entry’s strongest, most relevant analytical deliverable.

items.says: “Its benchmark” does not identify the index or benchmark type.
The cash forecast and debt-repayment claim is wrongly duplicated under a later manufacturing role.
items.because: The matching figures cannot be credited to unrelated roles years apart, and the treasury outcome conflicts with the student-fund context.

items.says: The cash-forecast bullet does not identify the forecasting approach.
items.because: The deliverable alone provides little evidence of forecasting skill.

items.says: The USD 600M measure and forecast-error calculation are undefined.
items.because: The ambiguities prevent the reader from interpreting or checking the claimed scale and accuracy.
